en.name: Clare of Montefalco
en.summary: Italian Augustinian abbess whose heart, examined after her death, was reported to contain tiny natural formations resembling the instruments of Christ's Passion.
en.body: Clare of Montefalco entered religious life as a child alongside her sister, eventually becoming abbess of an Augustinian community in the Italian hill town of Montefalco, where she was known for intense mystical prayer centered on the suffering of Christ and reported visions in which she felt Christ had planted his cross within her own heart. After her death in 1308, her sisters, following her own repeated statements that they would find something remarkable there, opened her body for embalming and reported discovering within the tissue of her heart small natural formations that appeared to resemble a miniature crucifix, a scourge, and other symbols of the Passion, an examination witnessed and documented by numerous townspeople and later investigated by Church authorities over an extended canonical process. Her heart, along with these findings, remains preserved and displayed at the monastery in Montefalco to this day. She was canonized in 1881, and her case remains one of the more closely documented reported bodily phenomena in the history of Catholic sainthood.
